findings.title: Workflow reminder cancellation is not awaited in cancel handler
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async, but they are fired inside a `forEach` without being collected into `prismaPromises` or awaited. The previous code collected `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` promises and awaited them before returning. Because this handler returns after `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`, the DB update that sets `cancelled = true` (or the SMS row deletion) may not complete before the serverless function is frozen after the response. A cancelled booking can therefore still have its scheduled email/SMS reminder sent.

findings.title: Reschedule path bypasses deferred cancellation and leaves stale reminder rows
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` calls SendGrid immediately with `status: 'cancel'`. This is the same pattern the PR says caused the 100 pending cancellation limit: it creates a SendGrid pending cancellation until the original send date. For rescheduled bookings, the new `cancelled`/cron mechanism should be used instead. In addition, the `immediateDelete` branch returns without deleting or marking the `WorkflowReminder` DB row, so the original booking retains rows that still appear scheduled and may be retried later. The promise is also not awaited.

findings.title: Request-reschedule workflow reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async and are called in a `forEach` without being awaited. The old code collected and awaited `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` promises. The mutation continues to send the reschedule request and returns; in a serverless environment the process can be frozen before the deferred `cancelled = true` update is written. The old workflow reminders can then still fire after the booking was put into the reschedule path.

findings.title: Workflow update cancels reminders without awaiting DB writes
findings.body: `remindersToDelete.flat().forEach(...)` calls the async managers without awaiting them, and the later `userWorkflow.steps.map(async (oldStep) => ...)` promises are also never awaited. The mutation subsequently updates the workflow and returns, so email/SMS cancellation calls and related DB deletes/updates can still be in flight. A cancelled reminder may be re-created or the old reminder may remain uncancelled, allowing emails/SMS from a disabled or edited workflow to be sent after the update completes.

findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancellation prevents deletion of already-cancelled rows
findings.body: The loop awaits each `client.request` sequentially and only afterwards calls `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. If any later SendGrid request throws, the `catch` runs before the delete promises are awaited, so rows for which cancellation already succeeded are not deleted. They remain `cancelled = true` and are retried on the next cron run, generating duplicate SendGrid cancellation requests and keeping stale rows until a run with no cancellation failures. The delete should be awaited immediately after a successful cancellation or the final `Promise.all` should run in a `finally`.

findings.title: Paid bookings return before scheduled workflow reminders are cancelled
findings.body: When `bookingToDelete.paid` is true, the handler refunds the payment, marks the booking REJECTED, and returns at this line. This is before the block at lines 484-493 that cancels scheduled workflow reminders. As a result, paid/rejected bookings with scheduled workflow reminders will still have those reminder emails/SMS sent after cancellation. This path is not covered by the PR's cancellation fix.
